issue.title: 3.8: Point CI test job at coverage output
issue.body_excerpt: Either run test:coverage or stop uploading coverage/.

affected_files.role: primary - fix the test job: change npm run test:run -> test:coverage (preferred) OR remove the 'Upload test coverage' step that uploads coverage/ which is never produced
no edit needed; test:coverage is already defined (vitest --run --coverage)

analysis.current_implementation: ci.yml test job runs `npm run test:run` (= `vitest --run`), which never invokes the coverage provider. The next step is 'Upload test coverage' which uses actions/upload-artifact@v4 with path: coverage/ — but that directory is never created. The artifact upload silently produces an empty archive on every CI run, wasting runner time and creating a misleading 'test-results' artifact in Actions that contains no coverage data.
analysis.limitations: Misleading CI signal: the artifact name 'test-results' is uploaded but is empty. The acceptance criterion is to either run test:coverage (so the upload is meaningful) or remove the upload step.
analysis.change_surface: 1 file. One-line change in the run command, or remove one step.
analysis.root_cause: The test job is configured to upload coverage/ but the test command does not produce it. This is a wiring bug introduced when the test job was authored without matching the package.json scripts.

options.name: Switch to test:coverage and keep the upload
options.summary: Change `npm run test:run` to `npm run test:coverage` in the test job, rename the artifact to 'coverage', and keep the upload step.
pros: Gives CI real coverage data; aligns with the existing test:coverage script
Acceptance criterion satisfied with a one-line diff
cons: Adds coverage report generation time per CI run (seconds)
options.risk_details: test:coverage is already defined and exercised locally; no new dependency required (@vitest/coverage-v8 is already a devDependency).

options.name: Drop the upload step
options.summary: Remove the 'Upload test coverage' step entirely. Keep test:run (faster, no coverage data on CI).
pros: Smallest diff; no extra CI time
cons: Loses any future intent to expose coverage in CI

options_considered: Switch to test:coverage and keep the upload
options_rejected: Drop the upload step (loses the coverage signal the project clearly wanted; prefer Option 1)

decision_record.root_cause: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `npm run test:run` (no coverage provider) but the following step uploads path: coverage/, which is never created. Result: an empty 'test-results' artifact on every CI run.
options_considered: Switch to test:coverage and keep the upload
decision_record.selected_option: Switch to test:coverage and keep the upload
decision_record.residual_risk: test:coverage adds seconds to each CI run; verify the budget is acceptable. If not, fall back to Option 2.
